# adds_wmi_filter (Resource)

Manages a WMI filter (an `msWMI-Som` object). WMI filters are assigned to GPOs with [`adds_gpo_wmi_filter`](../resources/gpo_wmi_filter.md).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "adds_wmi_filter" "windows_server_2022" {
  name        = "Windows Server 2022 only"
  description = "Applies GPOs only to Windows Server 2022 machines"

  queries = [
    {
      namespace = "root\\CIMv2"
      query     = "SELECT * FROM Win32_OperatingSystem WHERE Version LIKE \"10.0.20348%\" AND ProductType = \"3\""
    }
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name of the WMI filter. Changing this replaces the filter.
- `queries` (Attributes List) WQL queries the filter evaluates. A target matches the filter only if every query matches (GPMC ANDs them together). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--queries))

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of the WMI filter.

### Read-Only

- `distinguished_name` (String) Distinguished name of the WMI filter object.
- `id` (String) GUID of the WMI filter.

<a id="nestedatt--queries"></a>
### Nested Schema for `queries`

Required:

- `query` (String) WQL query text, for example `SELECT * FROM Win32_OperatingSystem WHERE Version LIKE "10.%"`.

Optional:

- `namespace` (String) WMI namespace the query runs against. Defaults to `root\CIMv2`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# WMI filters are imported by GUID.
terraform import adds_wmi_filter.windows_server_2022 "12345678-90ab-cdef-1234-567890abcdef"
```
